summary: Over 14 days, mean glucose was 121.6 mg/dL with 86.0% time in range, 8.9% above range, and 5.1% below range. Afternoon local highs (especially 14:00-17:00) were often followed by evening and early-night lows. Carbs were not logged, the declared meal-strategy list was empty, and closed-loop samples showed COB 0, so meal insulin was delivered through always-on SMB and UAM rather than CR. Competing basal, ISF, dynISF, SMB, IOB, GLP-1, a mid-period profile switch, and a pump occlusion were not separable enough to support a profile value change.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage was good enough for pattern review. The selected AAPS profile object is complete and historically applicable. Therapy attribution is weaker because carbs, activity, and a full meal declaration are absent, and a mid-period profile switch plus u200-dilute labeling limit unit comparisons.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, 5-minute cadence, 0 invalid or duplicate entries. Treatments 2315, insulin 655 entries totaling 275.95 U. carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0. profile_context.historical_applicability yes. Events include 13 Aug profile switch to u200 dilute basal, GLP-1 1.25 mg notes, site and sensor changes, and 19 Aug occlusion plus pump error.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb amounts or timestamps, no activity log, only representative treatments and loop statuses, partial first and last days, dilute-insulin conversion not quantified.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is strong by TIR, but time below range is the binding safety constraint. Lows cluster in local 23:00-03:00 and around 18:00-19:00, often after afternoon highs and high IOB. This vetoes more overnight insulin, a tighter night target, and a shorter DIA until leftover IOB is separated from scheduled basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%, SD 39.7. Local hourly TBR: hour 1 18.5%, hour 19 15.3%, hours 0/2/3/23 about 10-11%. Extremes 41-42 and 290-293 mg/dL. Loop IOB samples reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U. Daily TBR was highest on 11 Aug 9.4%, 14 Aug 8.3%, and 18 Aug 12.8%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment records and no activity notes to explain evening drops.

analysis_steps.findings: Local 03:00-07:00 is the cleanest fasting-like window and is roughly matched by the overnight and early-morning basal steps. 23:00-02:00 is not a clean basal test because of evening IOB. The 16:00 basal valley of 0.5 U/h sits under the highest TAR hour and may be protective against later lows. The 08:00-10:00 rise is more consistent with unannounced breakfast than a proven 06:00-10:00 basal defect. Night target 90 mg/dL sits on top of high nocturnal TBR but is not isolated from leftover automation insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: Basal segments 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h. Targets 90 mg/dL at 00:00 and 23:00, 100 mg/dL at 08:00. Local 03:00-07:00 averages about 99-106 mg/dL with low TAR. Local 16:00 average 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1% TAR, then hour 19 TBR 15.3%. Temp basal representatives include both 0 U/h suspends and highs near 2.7-4 U/h.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview hypo veto; data_quality no carbs and 13 Aug profile switch.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot separate scheduled basal from SMB, UAM, dynISF, missed meals, GLP-1, and evening activity.

analysis_steps.findings: CR cannot be validated because no carb treatments used those segments. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is continuously rewritten by dynISF. Correction windows are contradictory once meals and IOB are allowed. DIA 10 h is long and more consistent with leftover evening IOB than with a need to shorten duration. u200 dilute blocks simple TDD-to-ISF rules.
analysis_steps.evidence: CR 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, and 12.6 g/U. ISF one segment 56 mg/dL/U. DIA 10 h, insulin type free_peak_oref. Zero carb treatments. All 24 therapy windows are Correction Bolus. Loop variable_sens about 28-124 versus profile 56.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets evening hypo versus afternoon high; later SMB and sensitivity stages.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal bolus amounts, no carb timing, no absorption records, unknown dilute conversion.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are internally consistent with an unannounced-meal design: always-on SMB, UAM on, and COB or after-carb SMB off. Live delivery is more aggressive than 15-20 minutes times scheduled basal, including 3-minute interval, microboluses about 0.3-0.4 U, and at least one UAM high-boost SMB. High temporary targets at 135 mg/dL should pause SMB and must not be read as CR failure. Afternoon UAM on a rise plus DIA 10 h is a better explanation of evening and night lows than an isolated basal hole.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true, uam_enabled true, smb_always_enabled true, smb_with_cob_enabled false, smb_after_carbs_enabled false, smb_with_temp_target_enabled true, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, interval 3 min, max SMB 15 min, max UAM SMB 20 min. Loop reasons show COB 0, UAM boosts, and insulinReq up to about 2.59 U. Temporary targets at 135 mg/dL on 17 and 18 Aug lasted 180 minutes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview; unused CR; daytime highs not labeled basal-only.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Custom reason-string boosts are not fully specified as inventory fields, so classic minute limits understate live aggression.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off. DynISF at 70% is the active sensitivity engine and explains why effective ISF looks weak at highs and strong in later hypos. Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are far above observed TDD and schedule; they were not binding at sampled IOB near 6 U and are unused headroom rather than the current TBR cause. Carb-absorption settings are idle with 0 g logged. Enabling Autosens target lowering is not supported given nocturnal TBR. Sensitivity_ratio 1 is a neutral live adjustment, not proof Autosens is running.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true, dynISF factor 70%, Autosens target raise and lower false. variable_sens 37.9 at BG 262 and 27.8 at BG 246. One enact clipped about 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4 U/h. min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 unused.
analysis_steps.dependencies: profile ISF and DIA entanglement; SMB cluster; u200 pump units.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No independent Autosens log; custom twin and backout text is not a standard inventory lever.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no representative declared prebolus or immediate bolus percent. Observed execution matches that emptiness: no meal boluses, only corrections, and UAM after the rise. Immediate bolus percent and prebolus minutes cannot be assessed as numbers. The recurring shape is late automation insulin, then 2-6 hour falls into evening and night TBR.
analysis_steps.evidence: analysis_context.meal_strategies empty. carb_treatment_entries empty. Therapy windows are all Correction Bolus from 0.05-2.4 U, including rises after small corrections at breakfast and midday and crashes after afternoon corrections.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused; SMB and UAM always-on; DIA 10 h; target 90 overnight.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absent declared prebolus_minutes and immediate_bolus_percent; no meal-linked bolus wizard records.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs were not declared and not present in telemetry. They are not equivalent to a pump extended bolus. Absorption settings cannot be tested. Glucose action time is visible only as UAM rises lasting about 1-3 hours. Meal composition is not in the package and is not inferred.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min null, no e-carb fields in analysis_context, COB 0 in loop samples. GLP-1 notes on 14, 17, and 20 Aug can shift absorption but do not create e-carb records.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absent e-carb amount, start offset, and duration fields.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked likely causes: first unlogged meals handled by always-on UAM and SMB plus dynISF compression; second leftover IOB from that path under DIA 10 h causing 18:00-03:00 TBR; third possible smaller contributions from night target 90 mg/dL and 19:00 basal 0.7 U/h; fourth 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h more likely protective than deficient. CR is unused and cannot explain the file. No single profile or AAPS value is isolated enough to change. Keep the profile and automation numbers, verify overnight on low-IOB evenings, then log carbs before any CR, e-carb, or one-knob automation review. Do not change basal, ISF, dynISF, and SMB together.
analysis_steps.evidence: Checkpoints 1-3 plus package hourly_glucose_local, glucose_summary, zero carbs, dynISF variable_sens range, high sampled IOB, and empty meal_strategies. Package values override any earlier wording that a basal or CR defect was proven.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Same unresolved meal, activity, dilute-unit, and mid-period event gaps that block a value change.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7% with good cadence supports hourly pattern review.
Time in range 86.0% with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local 03:00-07:00 is relatively stable with little TAR, suggesting the overnight-to-morning basal steps are not grossly mismatched in a fasting-like window.
The selected profile is complete, marked historically applicable, and internally consistent with an unannounced-meal UAM design.
High temporary targets at 135 mg/dL are aligned with SMB-off-on-high-TT, which is a useful safety brake.
DIA 10 h is conservative relative to documented 41-42 mg/dL lows.
issues: Time below range 5.1%, clustered in local 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00, including readings of 41-42 mg/dL.
Afternoon local TAR peak at 14:00-17:00 often precedes those lows, consistent with late UAM or SMB IOB rather than an isolated fasting defect.
No carb entries and an empty declared meal-strategy list, so CR, prebolus, immediate bolus percent, and e-carbs cannot be tested.
DynISF rewrites flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U to roughly 28-124, so ISF, SMB, and unlogged meals remain entangled.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are far above observed delivery and do not constrain stacking before the cap.
Mid-period profile switch, GLP-1 notes, u200 dilute labeling, and a 19 Aug occlusion reduce full-period attribution.

recommendations.title: Keep the basal profile and split overnight observation by evening IOB
recommendations.description: The cleanest fasting-like window is local 03:00-07:00 and does not show a clear basal hole. Early-night lows remain mixed with leftover UAM and SMB IOB, so no basal segment has isolated support for a new rate.

suggested_change.direction: Leave all scheduled basal rates unchanged and compare 23:00-02:00 versus 03:00-07:00 on nights after low evening IOB.

recommendations.title: Review at most one automation knob only after the basal observation and carb logging
recommendations.description: Always-on SMB, the 3-minute interval, UAM 20 minutes, and dynISF 70% are one aggression cluster that can explain afternoon highs then evening lows. Changing them together with basal or ISF would hide the cause. No single new automation number is isolated in this file.

suggested_change.direction: Keep current SMB and dynISF values now. If the afternoon-to-night pattern remains after carbs are logged and overnight IOB is reviewed, discuss only one of interval, UAM minutes, or dynISF factor.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep every current basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA value. The next concrete check is whether local 23:00-02:00 lows persist on nights with low evening IOB and no large afternoon UAM burst.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Local 03:00-07:00 is roughly matched, while 23:00-02:00 and 18:00-19:00 lows remain compatible with leftover SMB and UAM insulin, dynISF compression at afternoon peaks, DIA 10 h, GLP-1, and unlogged meals. No profile segment is cleanly separated from those effects, so a rate or ratio change is unsupported.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For several nights, record evening IOB around 18:00-21:00 local and compare subsequent 23:00-02:00 TBR with 03:00-07:00 stability.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hour 0-1 averages 90-93 mg/dL with 11-18% TBR, but this window follows afternoon-evening UAM and sampled IOB up to about 6 U. Uncertainty: leftover insulin versus scheduled 0.6 U/h is not split. Dependencies: SMB or UAM cluster, DIA 10 h, night target 90 mg/dL. A lower or higher midnight rate is unsupported.

Evidence: local 05:00 average 104.2 mg/dL, TAR 0%, TBR 4.8%. Uncertainty: residual overnight IOB can still be present. Dependencies: prior 00:00 basal and night target. No isolated under- or over-basal signal.

Evidence: local 06:00-07:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with TBR 1.3-2.5% and almost no TAR, so a strong dawn basal defect is not shown. Uncertainty: 21 Aug 06:19 local 42 mg/dL is a single extreme. Dependencies: 05:00 step and morning meals after 08:00. Keep 0.8 U/h.

Evidence: local 10:00 average 148 mg/dL and 20.2% TAR, but this follows the 08:00-09:00 rise with no carb records. Uncertainty: breakfast UAM is the competing explanation. Dependencies: unused CR 13.2 g/U, always-on SMB, target 100 mg/dL from 08:00. Not labeled a basal hole.

Evidence: this is the lowest basal during the highest TAR hour (local 16:00 average 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1% TAR) and sits before hour 19 TBR 15.3% and lows of 41 mg/dL. Uncertainty: the valley may already be protecting against evening crashes. Dependencies: UAM or SMB on the afternoon rise, 16:00 CR unused, dynISF. Raising this rate would add insulin in a hypo-adjacent window.

Evidence: local 18:00 average 124.2 mg/dL with mixed 11.9% TAR and 7.7% TBR. Uncertainty: this hour is a transition after afternoon IOB, not a fasting test. Dependencies: 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h and SMB cluster. No isolated change.

Evidence: local 19:00 has the second-worst TBR at 15.3% and clustered 41-48 mg/dL readings. Uncertainty: 0.7 U/h may contribute, but afternoon UAM, corrections, and DIA 10 h remain plausible. Dependencies: safety veto against more evening insulin and against changing basal with SMB at the same time. Keep until low-IOB evenings are observed.

Evidence: zero carb treatments and loop COB 0, so this ratio was not used. Uncertainty: night snacks cannot be confirmed or denied. Dependencies: UAM path, not wizard CR. Changing an unused ratio would not explain this dataset.
Evidence: no carb entries in this segment. Early-morning glucose is the stable basal window, not a CR test. Uncertainty: unused setting. Dependencies: meal logging. Keep.

Evidence: 08:00-10:00 rise occurs with no meal bolus and COB 0, so UAM, not 13.2 g/U, delivered meal insulin. Uncertainty: actual breakfast grams unknown. Dependencies: SMB always-on. Keep until carbs are logged.

Evidence: this is the strongest CR on paper but was unused while afternoon TAR and evening TBR were driven by corrections and UAM. Uncertainty: if meals were eaten, composition is unknown. Dependencies: 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h and dynISF. Keep.
Evidence: evening TBR with no carb records is an IOB and basal-target problem, not a CR test. Uncertainty: unused ratio. Dependencies: night target and leftover SMB. Keep.

Evidence: dynISF 70% produced variable_sens about 28-124, so live dosing did not use 56 alone. Correction windows both over- and under-fell. Uncertainty: u200 dilute blocks 1800-rule comparisons. Dependencies: dynISF, SMB, DIA. Changing ISF together with dynISF is not allowed; neither is isolated.

Evidence: overnight TBR is high under a 90 mg/dL target. Uncertainty: leftover IOB can create the same lows at a higher target, so this is not a proven target defect. Dependencies: safety veto against a tighter night target; SMB always-on. Raising the target is a possible later safety discussion, not a supported change from this file.

Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL coincides with afternoon TAR that is better explained by unlogged meals and UAM. Uncertainty: a lower daytime target would likely increase SMB, which conflicts with evening hypo risk. Dependencies: smb_always_enabled. Keep.
Evidence: local 23:00 TBR 10.1% as glucose falls into the night. Uncertainty: same IOB confound as the 00:00 target. Dependencies: 19:00 basal, DIA, SMB cluster. Keep pending the overnight IOB split.

Evidence: 2-6 hour crashes after afternoon UAM or corrections, plus lows of 41-42 mg/dL, fit a long insulin tail. Uncertainty: free_peak_oref peak shape is not independently measured. Dependencies: high evening IOB. Shortening DIA is unsupported and would hide active insulin.

Evidence: zero carbs and COB 0 mean UAM is the only observed meal path; disabling it would leave the 08:00-17:00 rises without a logged-carb alternative. Uncertainty: how much of TBR is UAM versus dynISF is unsplit. Dependencies: empty meal declaration and unused CR. Both source values are present, so verify is not used. Keep the pair together rather than inventing a one-sided switch.

Evidence: activation flags match unannounced meals and the 135 mg/dL high-TT SMB-off behavior. Uncertainty: always-on SMB is part of the aggression cluster. Dependencies: no carb logging yet. Source components are non-null. Keep rather than flip always-on without a meal-entry plan.

Uncertainty: no isolated test of interval versus UAM minutes versus dynISF. Dependencies: do not change delivery limits with ISF or basal in the same step. No new minute values are supported. Keep.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: observed TDD about 19.7 U/day pump units and peak sampled IOB about 6 U, so 25 U and 12 U/h were not binding; one path already clipped near 4 U/h. Uncertainty: unused headroom is a safety concern if stacking increases, but a specific tighter cap is not measured. Dependencies: dynISF and SMB, not current TBR cause. Keep; do not invent a new cap.

Evidence: dynISF 70% rewrote ISF at highs and is entangled with afternoon overshoot then night TBR. Autosens is off; sensitivity_ratio 1 is neutral, not disabled-Autosens proof. Uncertainty: 70% versus profile ISF 56 cannot be separated. Dependencies: do not change dynISF with profile ISF. Enabling Autosens target lowering would fight nocturnal TBR. Keep all listed components.
Evidence: both settings are idle with 0 g logged and COB 0. UAM rises are not COB double-counting. Uncertainty: absorption shape unknown. Dependencies: meal logging and unused CR. Keep.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: There is no declared prebolus, no declared immediate bolus percent, and no e-carbs. Observed meals are unannounced and covered after the rise by always-on SMB and UAM, with CR unused. Keep that combined approach until carb grams and clock times are logged; do not add e-carbs or invent a bolus percent from this file.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: User-declared meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, which matches telemetry of zero carb and e-carb entries. Afternoon TAR then 18:00-03:00 TBR fits late UAM or SMB IOB under DIA 10 h, not a documented under-prebolus of a known number of minutes.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carb grams and clock time for several usual meals, or fill meal_strategies with the actual prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percent, and e-carb duration if those are used.

exceptions.suggestion: Treat this window as high leftover-IOB risk rather than a CR or e-carb problem until meals are logged.
exceptions.rationale: This pattern is different from the milder 08:00-10:00 rise and collides with night target 90 mg/dL and DIA 10 h.

exceptions.suggestion: Do not read rises in those windows as CR failure, because high-TT SMB is disabled.

implementation_steps: Confirm the selected aaps_profile remains the one in use and note u200 dilute, GLP-1, site, sensor, and 19 Aug occlusion days when reviewing traces.
Leave all profile segments unchanged and first compare local 23:00-02:00 with 03:00-07:00 on nights after low evening IOB.
Log carb grams and time for usual meals, or record a non-empty meal-strategy declaration, before any CR or e-carb review.
If the afternoon-high then evening-low pattern remains after that observation, discuss only one automation item among SMB interval, UAM minutes, or dynISF factor.
Do not change basal, ISF, DIA, SMB delivery, and dynISF in the same step. Make at most one change, then monitor glucose closely.
education: Time in range can look strong while time below range still clusters overnight; those are different questions.
UAM is not a second COB counter. In this file COB stayed 0, so UAM was the meal path.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral live adjustment and does not mean Autosens is off; Autosens is off because autosens_enabled is false.
Dynamic ISF can make profile ISF 56 mg/dL/U look weak at highs and strong later, which is why ISF and dynISF should not be judged as one number.
E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus. No e-carb duration should be inferred from an aggregate average or from temp basal.
Remaining minutes on an SMB or low-temp message are not the configured 3-minute SMB interval.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice. The user must independently verify every proposed change with their care team.
Time below range was 5.1% with clustered readings of 41-42 mg/dL. Extra overnight insulin, a tighter night target, and a shorter DIA are not supported.
Sampled IOB reached about 4.7-5.9 U while max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h were not binding. Unused ceilings do not protect against stacking before the cap.
If any setting is later changed, change only one item, wait to observe, and monitor glucose closely. Do not change AAPS automatically from this review.
u200 dilute means all insulin units in this package are pump units and should not be converted with standard TDD rules.
